caption: The drawing depicts a coiled woven mat or rug seen from above, with the rolled edge on the left. The leftmost section is tan or light brown, with a rough texture and occasional white stitches running horizontally. There are two loose brownish, cloth-like strands draped over this section. Moving right, there is a vertical strip composed of blue, dark blue, and white alternating bands, followed by a much wider section dominated by a red and blue woven pattern with orange, white, and some dark blue and black elements forming a dense, grid-like texture. To the right of this central woven band are several narrower stripes in light green, yellow, white, some additional blue, and brown with visible weaving patterns. The right edge tapers off into shriveled, folded ends, similar to the left edge. The overall object sits on a cream or beige background, and the detail in the rendering shows shadows and fabric textures. There is a signature “Charles Goodwin” in the lower right corner.
title: Fragment of Shaker Hall Rug
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
